title: The Story of the Merchant and the Demon

paragraphs.en: Once upon a time, there was a wealthy merchant who traveled extensively. One day, he decided to visit another country with provisions in his saddlebag—bread and dates. After many days of travel, he reached his destination and completed his business.
paragraphs.zh: 从前，有一位四处经商的富商。一天，他决定带着褡裢里的干粮——面包和枣，前往另一个国家办理一些事务。经过长途跋涉，终于抵达目的地并完成了他的生意。

paragraphs.en: On the way back home, after three days, he stopped at an orchard for shade from the sun. He tied his horse by a spring under a walnut tree, ate some bread and dates, and threw the pits around.
paragraphs.zh: 回到家的路上，经过三天的旅程后，他停在一棵核桃树下的果园里避暑。他在一棵泉水边拴好了马，吃了一些面包和无花果，然后把果核随意扔在一旁。

paragraphs.en: The merchant was approached by an old demon wielding a sword. The demon stood with his feet on the ground but his head in the clouds, and demanded that the merchant rise so he could kill him, as the merchant had killed his son. Terrified, the merchant asked for clarification.
paragraphs.zh: 商人身处险境，面前站着一位手持利剑的老妖。妖魔双脚踏地，却仿佛心在九霄云外，他命令商人起身，好让他一剑封喉，因为是商人害死了他的儿子。商人惊恐万分，连忙求情问个明白。

paragraphs.en: The demon accused the merchant of killing his son while eating dates, causing one of the pits to strike and kill the boy.
paragraphs.zh: 恶魔指控商人在吃无花果时杀害了他的儿子，其中一个石块因此掉落，击杀了孩子。

paragraphs.en: The merchant pleaded for mercy, claiming it was an accident. He recited verses about life's dualities—peace and wariness, happiness and worry—and appealed to God’s justice. As he spoke, the demon raised his sword again.
paragraphs.zh: 商人在恳求饶恕，声称这纯属意外。他吟诵着关于人生两面性的诗句——和平与警觉、快乐与忧虑，并祈求上帝的公正。就在这时，恶魔再次举起了他的剑。

paragraphs.en: The merchant wept, beseeching forgiveness from God.
paragraphs.zh: 商人在祈求上帝的宽恕，泪水不禁滑下了脸颊。

paragraphs.en: The merchant pleaded with the demon, "Must you kill me?" The demon replied, "I must." But Shahrazad interrupted as morning approached.
paragraphs.zh: 商人在恶魔面前哀求：“你非杀我不可吗？”恶魔回答道：“是的。”但沙海拉罕在晨光熹微时打断了他们。

paragraphs.en: She and her sister Dinarzad continued their conversation, with Dinarzad praising the story and Shahrazad promising an even better one later.
paragraphs.zh: 她和妹妹迪纳兹达继续交谈，迪纳兹达称赞起这个故事来，沙赫拉扎德则承诺稍后会为大家带来一个更精彩的故事。

paragraphs.en: King Shahrayar, intrigued, decided to spare Shahrazad until he heard more. The next day, the king returned home and asked for the demon's tale to be completed. Shahrazad agreed happily.
paragraphs.zh: 国王沙哈拉叶尔饶有兴趣，决定先让莎赫拉兹德继续她的故事。第二天，国王回到家中，催促她讲完妖魔的故事。莎赫拉兹德欣然应允。

paragraphs.en: On the second night, the merchant begged for time: "Please let me say goodbye to my family and divide my property." The demon feared he would not return. The merchant swore by God that he would come back on New Year’s Day if released.
paragraphs.zh: 第二个晚上，商人大声哀求：“求您让我和家人告别，并分配我的财产。”恶魔担心他此去不再回来。商人在神明面前发誓，如果获释，他会新年第一天返回。

paragraphs.en: The demon agreed, setting a year's deadline.
paragraphs.zh: 恶魔同意了，并设定了一个一年的期限。

paragraphs.en: The merchant returned home after his encounter with the demon. Upon seeing his wife and children, he wept bitterly. His family's concern only deepened their sorrow.
paragraphs.zh: 商人在与恶魔相遇后回到了家中，见到妻子和孩子们，不禁悲从中来。家人的担忧反而加深了他们的悲伤。

paragraphs.en: His wife asked why he mourned when they were celebrating his return. He replied that he had only one year left to live.
paragraphs.zh: 他的妻子问他为何在庆祝归来的喜事时还伤心不已。他回答说，自己只剩下一年的寿命了。

paragraphs.en: Everyone cried upon hearing this. His wife struck her face in grief, cut her hair, while his daughters wailed and children wept. The day turned into a somber farewell as the family gathered around their father.
paragraphs.zh: 听到这话，所有人都悲痛不已。他的妻子捶胸顿足，剪断了头发；女儿们哭泣不止，孩子们也泪眼婆娑。这一天变成了沉重的送别，全家人都围在父亲身边。

paragraphs.en: The next day, the merchant wrote his will, dividing his property and freeing his slaves. He appointed guardians for his young ones and distributed gifts to his wife according to their marriage contract. He spent time with his family until New Year's Day approached.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天，商人在临终前写下了遗嘱，将财产作了分配，并解放了他的奴隶。他为年幼的孩子们指定监护人，并根据婚约向妻子赠送了礼物。他在与家人共度时光，直到新年的钟声即将敲响。

paragraphs.en: On that day, he performed his ablutions and prayers, then carried his burial shroud as he bid farewell to his family. His sons clung to him, daughters wept, and his wife wailed. Their mourning moved him to tears.
paragraphs.zh: 那天，他先完成了净身和祈祷，然后抱着棺材与家人告别。孩子们紧紧依偎着他，女儿们哭泣，妻子悲痛欲绝。他们的哀伤让他也不禁落泪。

paragraphs.en: He embraced and kissed them goodbye, saying, "This is God's will." Then he mounted his horse and journeyed day and night until he reached the orchard on New Year’s Day.
paragraphs.zh: 他拥抱他们，吻别道：“这是上帝的旨意。”然后跨上马背，日夜兼程，终于在除夕那天赶到了果园。

paragraphs.en: He sat where he had eaten dates, waiting for the demon, his heart heavy and eyes filled with tears. An old man approached, leading a deer on a leash, and greeted him. The merchant replied, recounting his tale from beginning to end.
paragraphs.zh: 他坐在曾吃枣子的地方，等待着恶魔的到来，心中沉重，眼里含着泪光。一位老人牵着一只鹿走近，向他打了声招呼。商人口中吐露着自己的遭遇，从头到尾地诉说着。

paragraphs.en: Impressed by his fidelity, the old man said, "Your pledge is magnificent." He vowed not to leave until he saw what would happen between them.
paragraphs.zh: 老者被他的忠诚所打动，说道：“你的誓言真是掷地有声。”他发誓一定要亲眼见证他们之间会发生什么。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent as dawn broke. Her sister Dinarzad remarked, "What a strange and wonderful story!" Shahrazad replied, "Tomorrow night I will tell something even stranger."
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹阿德默然不语。她的妹妹丁纳札德remarked道：“这真是一个奇异而美妙的故事！”沙赫拉兹阿德回答说：“明天晚上我将讲述更加奇异的事情。”

paragraphs.en: On the third night, when it was dark and Shahrazad lay with the king, her sister requested, “Please, if you are not sleepy, tell us one of your lovely tales to pass the night.” The king added, “Let it be about the conclusion of the merchant’s story.”
paragraphs.zh: 第三晚，在夜色中，沙哈拉兹德与国王同眠时，她的妹妹请求道：“如果你不困，请给我们讲一个你那动人的故事吧，以打发这个夜晚。”国王补充说：“最好是关于商人故事的结局。”

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad agreed: As the merchant and the man with the deer sat talking, another old man approached, followed by two black hounds. He greeted them, and they returned his greeting. The old man inquired about their stories, and the man with the deer recounted how the merchant had sworn to return on New Year’s Day, only for the demon to wait to kill him.
paragraphs.zh: 沙赫拉兹阿德同意了：商人与那名驯鹿主人正坐着交谈时，一位老者带着两只黑色猎犬走近。他向他们问好，两人也回以问候。老者询问起他们的故事，那名驯鹿主人讲述了商人曾发誓会在新年那天回来，结果恶魔却守在那里等他来杀人的事情。

paragraphs.en: Both the old man and the man with the dogs were amazed and swore never to leave until they saw what would happen between them.
paragraphs.zh: 老人和牵狗的人既惊讶又发誓，除非亲眼看到他们之间会发生什么，否则绝不会离开。

paragraphs.en: A third old man approached and greeted them. He inquired about their somber demeanor and learned that they were waiting for a demon to decide the merchant's fate. Moved by the story, he joined them, vowing not to leave until he saw what would happen.
paragraphs.zh: 一个年迈的老者走近，向他们问好。他询问起他们为何神情凝重，得知他们在等待恶魔决定商人的命运后，被这个故事所触动，加入了他们的行列，并发誓不看到事情的结果绝不离开。

paragraphs.en: Suddenly, dust rose from the open country, clearing to reveal the approaching demon with a sword drawn. He ignored greetings, yanked the merchant, and declared that death was imminent. The merchant and the three old men wept.
paragraphs.zh: 突然，尘土从旷野中扬起，渐渐散去，露出一个手持利剑的恶魔正缓缓逼近。他 ignore 了问候，一把抓住商人，断言死亡迫在眉睫。商人和那三位老人不禁泪流满面。

paragraphs.en: Dawn broke, and Shahrazad paused her tale. Dinarzad praised it, but Shahrazad hinted at an even better story to come if she were spared. The king, intrigued, decided not to execute her until he heard more of the story.
paragraphs.zh: 黎明到来，沙赫拉兹暂停了她的故事。丁纳扎德称赞她，但沙赫拉兹暗示如果自己能免于一死，将有一个更加精彩的故事。国王被激起兴趣，决定暂不执行死刑，先听听更多的故事。

paragraphs.en: The next morning, the king attended to his kingdom and then visited Shahrazad's father, treating him kindly. That night, in bed with Shahrazad, Dinarzad urged her to continue the tale. With pleasure, she began again:
paragraphs.zh: 第二天一早，国王处理完国事，随后拜访了沙哈拉兹德的父亲，待他十分友善。当晚与沙哈拉兹德共枕而眠时，迪纳尔扎德催促她继续讲述故事。沙哈拉兹德欣然应允，重新开始了她的讲述：

paragraphs.en: The Fourth Night
paragraphs.zh: 第四夜

paragraphs.en: O happy King, an elderly man with a deer approached the demon. Kissing his hands and feet, he said, "Demon king, if I tell you my story and yours to the merchant seems strange, will you grant me a third of your claim on him?" The demon agreed, "I will."
paragraphs.zh: 幸福的国王啊，一位白发苍苍、身着鹿皮衣的老人走近了恶魔。他吻着恶魔的手和脚，说道：“恶魔陛下，如果我讲述我的故事以及您的故事，而商人的反应显得有些奇怪，您是否会赐给我您对他的三分之一财产权利？”恶魔答应了，“我会的。”
